title: Ghaṭakarpara-kāvya — with Vivṛti commentary
author: Anonymous (transmitted under Bhartṛhari's name in some manuscripts)
text:
The Ghaṭakarpara is a short kāvya of some twenty verses, among the most piquant survivors of early Sanskrit court poetry, transmitted with Bhartṛhari's name in some manuscripts but widely regarded by scholars as the work of an unknown hand — an early composition, later furnished with a vivṛti commentary that our text carries with it. Its subject is śṛṅgāra: desire and its absence played as a single event. The separated lover, the lightning-flash of meeting, the vexation that is indistinguishable from delight — all are performed rather than described.

Its juice: the poem's famous paradoxes (the pain that is sought, the night brighter than day) are not ornaments pasted onto feeling; they are the argument. In Ghaṭakarpara, erotic experience is shown to already contain its own inversion, and that inverted structure is what makes it poetry.
